answer: Mint one nontransferable capacity ticket only after a key completes a paid task accepted by a distinct customer; a new identity must burn one ticket at activation, and the contract rejects any reused ticket. A proposed 0.03 POA verification fee per ticket (not a current protocol rule) means 1,000 fake keys cost 1,000 × 0.03 = 30 POA; one honest key pays 0.03 POA once. A sample task could map juniper vines on an island. This ties key growth to proven service, but colluding customers can still manufacture acceptance.
